detection.quote: If a marking tutor suspects academic misconduct in your coursework they will send written details to the Associate Dean for the Faculty
you may be required to attend an Academic Conduct Interview to allow you an opportunity to demonstrate that the work is your own
The Academic Conduct Officer may ask you to provide your notes, drafts, and any other records relating to your preparatory work for the assessment.

process.quote: If a marking tutor suspects academic misconduct in your coursework they will send written details to the Associate Dean for the Faculty
a full investigation, conducted by the Associate Dean appointed Academic Conduct Officer, will now commence
You will be given time and opportunity to respond to any allegation.
An Academic Conduct Panel shall be convened at the earliest opportunity if you have denied the allegations or where the appropriate sanction indicated by the investigation falls under Levels 2 to 4.

If you do not appear at the Panel, the Panel may proceed to deal with the allegation in your absence provided the Chair of the Panel is satisfied that you have been properly notified of the sitting of the Panel.

You have a right to be accompanied to the Panel by a member of the University community to support you who must be independent of the allegation and may be a fellow student, an Officer or staff member advocate from the Students’ Union.
Appeals against process followed, and/or sanctions set should be submitted in writing to academic.integrity@winchester.ac.uk
Investigations should take no more than 15 working days
Investigations will be determined on a ‘balance of probability’ basis
Your academic record will then be updated with a Level One outcome.

outcomes.quote: Requirement for Additional Learning and 10% Grade Penalty (for graded work)*
Requirement for Additional Learning and to resubmit a new piece of work for capped grades
Requirement for Additional Learning and to resubmit a new piece of work for capped grades
Termination of programme registration and/or withdrawal from the University
the reclassification or revocation of award will be approved by Senate under the authority of the Vice Chancellor or nominee.
You can be investigated even after you have been awarded your degree.
a sanction above that previously applied will be levied where it is determined by the investigation and panel that the further offence is an escalation of misconduct.

The proportion of the work affected by the misconduct, the potential contribution of the affected work towards the overall mark, opportunities for prior feedback relating to the offences, the number of previous and contemporaneous offences and the existence of evidence of intention to deceive or coerce.

The University retains the right to disclose proven breaches against you and any penalties and sanctions to professional bodies, where it is necessary and appropriate to do so under the requirements of professional registration.

definitions.quote: Plagiarism is when you use someone else’s work, ideas, words or intellectual property in your work without giving them appropriate acknowledgement, i.e. referencing correctly.
Self-plagiarism is when you re-use your own work without permission or acknowledgement.
Cheating is when you deceitfully or fraudulently obtain an unfair advantage in an assessment, for instance by bringing unauthorised materials into an exam venue.

Collusion is when you work with another student/s or other individuals in an unauthorised way to create a piece of assessed work where the expectation is that the submitted work should be solely your own and created by yourself.

Contract cheating, sometimes referred to as ‘ghosting’ or ‘passing off’, is when you commission a third party to produce work, whole or in parts, which you declare as your own work through the submission process.
Falsification is when you attempt to present fictitious or distorted material contributing to an assessment or falsify evidence to support special considerations
Personation is the assumption by one person of the identity of another person with intent to deceive or to gain unfair advantage.
